A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TokMem research. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, figures, and the 1,000-task list, support reliable comparison despite renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on SNI, APIGen, Fanfics, and GSM8K, including routing, compositional generalization, forgetting, and memory-placement results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds an empirical analysis of memory-token embedding norms in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: The memory bank, next-token objective, frozen backbone, renormalization, decoupled variant, and auxiliary compositional adaptation procedure are retained. The new inference subsection explains existing routing and generation behavior rather than establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SNI tasks, APIGen tools, Fanfics memorization setting, and GSM8K reasoning task. The complete SNI task list is identical. The new norm analysis examines the existing continual tool-learning setting without expanding task or population coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baselines: Base, RAG, LoRA, and replay for atomic recall; ICL, RAG, and LoRA for compositional recall; and prefix tuning for placement studies. Table 3 renames and reorders the existing adapted and unadapted TokMem variants.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 changes the reported LoRA target projections from query/key in v1 to query/value in v2. This is a stated configuration revision, without evidence that experiments were rerun. Model sizes, principal training budgets, sample counts, and benchmark metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds Appendix B.2 and Figure 6, measuring embedding norms as ten new tools are introduced in each of five rounds without renormalization. This directly examines the proposed norm-inflation mechanism. Existing compositional-generalization, forgetting, freezing, and placement analyses are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: New Figure 6 reports standard deviations across the ten newly added memory tokens in each round. These describe variation across tokens, not repeated training runs. The existing five-run averaging for the Fanfics experiment is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds measured evidence of overall norm inflation across training rounds. Existing performance-table values are unchanged after matching moved tables and reordered adaptation rows, and the retained performance plots contain identical images. No new benchmark performance gain is reported.

T1.justification: The underlying mathematical model, training losses, and renormalization rule are unchanged. v2's explicit softmax routing expression restates existing next-token selection, while other equation changes concern notation and presentation. No new theoretical result, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction temper v1's broad claim of surpassing fine-tuning to matching or exceeding it, particularly for compositional recall. The central contribution remains compact procedural tokens supporting selective recall, composition, and continual acquisition with a frozen backbone.

C2.justification: Appendix C explicitly identifies dependence on manually curated, procedurally decomposed training data as a bottleneck and proposes teacher-generated query decomposition. This expands v1's general limitations about realistic procedures and richer composition. The earlier explicit caveat about unexplored multi-turn interactions is omitted.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code link, explicitly describes argmax routing and possible ordinary-text fallback, and discloses within-task shuffling. Conversely, Appendix A.3 omits the explicit 9:1 APIGen split ratio stated in v1 Appendix D.2. Core hardware and optimization details remain available.

R1.justification: Section 4 expands comparisons with Flora, Mixture-of-LoRAs, gist tokens, and context compression. Additional citations support norm inflation and memory capacity, while the minimum-description-length motivation and citation disappear. These refine the existing positioning rather than redefine the contribution.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting spans the abstract, introduction, method explanation, and experimental discussion. v2 adds a dedicated inference subsection, moves compositional generalization into the appendix, reorganizes experimental details and supplementary results, and separates future work from the shortened conclusion. The title also changes from Tokenized to One-Token Procedural Memory.

P2.justification: v2 adds the norm plot, relocates the compositional-generalization table to Appendix B.1, and revises its headers and highlighting. Table 3 gains explicit adaptation labels and reordered rows; Figure 5 changes addressing terminology to indexing. Other displays receive limited resizing, caption edits, and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The new norm analysis provides direct support for the stability mechanism, while clearer inference documentation, explicit data-curation limitations, and a code link improve transparency. These are useful but bounded gains because the method and benchmark results remain unchanged. Omitting the explicit APIGen split ratio and introducing parameter-count comparability wording that is difficult to reconcile with Table 3 weaken protocol clarity, but do not outweigh the improvements.
